en: 2 eggs
100 g cooked Japanese rice
1 tsp soy sauce
1 tsp mirin
1 tsp oil
Beat the eggs with the soy sauce and mirin
Oil a rectangular pan and heat it
Pour a thin layer and roll it once set
Repeat the layers, slice and serve with rice

serving.en: One bowl (50 g natto + 150 g rice)

en: 1 pack natto (50 g)
150 g cooked Japanese rice
1 tsp soy sauce
Chopped spring onion
1 sheet nori, shredded
Stir the natto with chopsticks about 20 times until creamy
Add the soy sauce and stir again
Put hot rice in a bowl and spoon the natto over
Top with spring onion and nori

name.en: Miso Soup with Tofu and Wakame, with Rice

en: Water 300 ml and dashi stock (or a light stock cube)
Miso paste 2 tbsp
Soft tofu, cubed, 60 g
Dried wakame 1 tsp
Chopped spring onion for garnish
Cooked white rice 100 g
Heat the water with the dashi until near boiling, without a hard boil.
Dissolve the miso paste in a ladle of the hot stock, then return it to the pot (avoid boiling the miso directly so it doesn't lose its flavour).
Add the tofu and dried wakame and let it sit two minutes until the wakame softens.
Pour into a serving bowl, garnish with spring onion, and serve with the rice.

name.en: Okayu (Japanese Rice Porridge) with Pickled Plum

en: White rice 40 g
Water 400 ml
1 umeboshi (Japanese pickled plum)
Chopped spring onion for garnish
A little salt
Toasted sesame seeds (optional)
Wash the rice thoroughly and place it with the water in a pot.
Cook over very low heat 35-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice breaks down and the texture becomes creamy.
Add a little salt to taste if desired.
Pour into a serving bowl, place the umeboshi in the centre, and garnish with spring onion and sesame.

name.en: Grilled Salted Cod with Rice and Pickled Cucumber

en: White fish fillet (cod or haddock) 120 g
A little salt
Cooked white rice 120 g
Thinly sliced cucumber 50 g
Rice vinegar 1 tsp and salt for a quick pickle
Sesame seeds for garnish
Sprinkle salt over the fish and let it sit 10 minutes.
Grill under the broiler or in a 220°C oven 8-10 minutes until cooked and it flakes easily.
For the pickle: sprinkle a little salt over the cucumber and let it sit 5 minutes, squeeze out the excess water, add the rice vinegar and toss.
Serve the fish with the rice and pickled cucumber, garnish with sesame.

name.en: Tamago Kake Gohan (Raw Egg over Rice)

en: Hot cooked white rice 150 g
1 fresh, high-quality egg
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tsp
Chopped spring onion for garnish
Shredded nori (dried seaweed) (optional)
Sesame seeds (optional)
Put the hot rice into a serving bowl.
Crack the egg into a separate small bowl and confirm it is fresh.
Pour the egg directly over the hot rice, add the soy sauce.
Mix well until the rice is coated with the egg, garnish with spring onion, nori and sesame, and serve immediately.
Boiled dried shirasu or small anchovies 40 g
Cooked white rice 150 g
Chopped spring onion
A light drizzle of low-sodium soy sauce
Grated ginger
Sesame seeds and shredded nori for garnish
Put the hot rice into a serving bowl.
Arrange the shirasu over the rice.
Drizzle with the light soy sauce and grated ginger.
Garnish with spring onion, sesame and nori, and serve immediately.
Cooked white rice 150 g
Miso paste 1 tbsp
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tsp
Half a tsp brown sugar
Sesame seeds for garnish
1 tsp oil for brushing
Mix the miso with the soy sauce and brown sugar until combined.
Shape the warm rice into two triangular or round balls with wet hands, pressing firmly to hold together.
Heat a non-stick pan and brush the rice with the miso mixture on both sides.
Grill 3-4 minutes per side until golden and crisp on the outside, sprinkle with sesame and serve hot.
Cooked white rice 150 g
Furikake seasoning (sesame, seaweed and dried fish mix) 2 tbsp
2 sheets nori (dried seaweed)
A little salt
Extra sesame seeds (optional)
Mix the hot rice with the furikake seasoning and a little salt until evenly distributed.
Wet your hands and sprinkle a little salt on them.
Shape the rice into two triangles or balls, pressing firmly to hold together.
Wrap each with a sheet of nori, sprinkle extra sesame if desired, and serve immediately.
Cooked white rice 150 g
Hot Japanese green tea (sencha) 200 ml
1 umeboshi (Japanese pickled plum)
Shredded nori
Chopped spring onion
Sesame seeds
Put the hot rice into a serving bowl.
Place the umeboshi in the centre and sprinkle with nori, spring onion and sesame.
Pour the hot green tea directly over the rice.
Serve immediately and stir lightly before eating.

serving.en: 100 g salmon + 150 g rice + miso soup

en: 100 g salmon fillet
Half tsp salt
150 g cooked Japanese rice
1 tsp miso paste
Tofu, wakame, spring onion for the soup
Salt the salmon, rest 15 minutes, then pat it dry
Grill 6 minutes per side until the skin crisps
Heat the soup water and dissolve the miso off the boil
Add tofu and wakame, serve with the rice
100 g soba noodles
Half cup dashi stock
2 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp mirin
Spring onion, wasabi, nori
Mix the dashi, soy sauce and mirin, then chill
Boil the soba for the time on the packet
Rinse under cold water until firm
Serve on a bamboo tray with the dipping sauce and toppings
Chicken breast, flattened, 150 g
Coarse breadcrumbs 30 g
1 beaten egg
1 tbsp whole-wheat flour
Cooked white rice 120 g
Salt, black pepper and a little tonkatsu sauce or soy sauce to serve
Season the chicken with salt and black pepper.
Coat it in the flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs, pressing lightly to adhere.
Arrange on a lined tray and mist lightly with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp, slice and serve with the rice and sauce.
Chicken breast, small pieces, 120 g
2 lightly beaten eggs
1 medium onion, sliced
Cooked white rice 130 g
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and water 80 ml
1 tsp brown sugar and spring onion for garnish
Simmer the onion in the soy sauce, water and brown sugar for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the chicken and cook 5-6 minutes until done.
Pour the beaten egg evenly over the chicken and onion, cover and cook 1 to 1.5 minutes until the egg sets slightly while staying a bit soft.
Pour it over the rice in a serving bowl, garnish with spring onion, and serve hot.
Very thinly sliced lean beef 120 g
1 large onion, thinly sliced
Cooked white rice 130 g
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and water 100 ml
Brown sugar 2 tsp and mirin 1 tsp (optional)
Pickled ginger and spring onion for garnish
Put the onion in a pan with the soy sauce, water, brown sugar and mirin, cook 5 minutes until the onion softens.
Add the beef slices and spread them out so they don't clump, cook 3-4 minutes until fully done.
Let the liquid reduce slightly over medium heat 2-3 minutes until it thickens.
Pour it over the rice in a serving bowl, garnish with pickled ginger and spring onion, and serve hot.
Chicken breast, small pieces, 120 g
Potato, carrot and onion, chopped, 150 g total
Cooked white rice 120 g
1 tbsp whole-wheat flour
1 tbsp curry powder and 1 tsp oil
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tsp and water 300 ml
Heat the oil and stir the chicken and onion until the chicken changes colour and the onion softens.
Add the potato and carrot and stir for two minutes.
Add the water, cover and simmer 15 minutes until the vegetables are cooked.
Dissolve the flour and curry powder in a little cold water and add to the pot along with the soy sauce, cook 5 more minutes until the sauce thickens, and serve over the rice.
Fresh or dried udon noodles 120 g
Dashi stock or light chicken stock 400 ml
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and mirin 1 tsp
Peeled shrimp 80 g and mixed vegetables for tempura (bell pepper, aubergine) 60 g
Coarse breadcrumbs 30 g and 1 beaten egg
Chopped spring onion for garnish
Coat the shrimp and vegetables in the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Arrange on a lined tray and bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
Boil the udon noodles according to the package instructions, drain.
Heat the dashi with the soy sauce and mirin until it boils, pour it over the noodles in a serving bowl, arrange the tempura on top and garnish with spring onion.

name.en: Katsudon (Pork Cutlet and Egg Rice Bowl)

en: Flattened pork or chicken cutlet 140 g
Coarse breadcrumbs 30 g, 1 egg for coating and 1 tbsp flour
2 eggs for the sauce
1 small onion, sliced
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp, water 80 ml and brown sugar 1 tsp
Cooked white rice 130 g
Coat the cutlet in flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp, slice into strips.
Simmer the onion in the soy sauce, water and brown sugar for 3 minutes, add the sliced cutlet.
Pour the beaten eggs over it, cover and cook 1 to 1.5 minutes until the egg sets slightly, pour it over the rice and serve hot.

name.en: Yakisoba (Stir-Fried Noodles with Pork and Vegetables)

en: Soba noodles or ready-made stir-fry noodles 140 g
Lean pork or chicken, thin slices, 90 g
Cabbage, carrot and spring onion, chopped, 150 g total
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and Worcestershire sauce 1 tsp (or balsamic vinegar as an alternative)
Brown sugar 1 tsp and 1 tsp oil
Aonori seaweed flakes and pickled ginger for garnish
Heat the oil and stir the meat until it changes colour and is cooked through.
Add the cabbage and carrot and stir 3-4 minutes until the vegetables soften.
Add the noodles, soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce and brown sugar, toss well until the noodles absorb the flavour (3-4 minutes).
Add the spring onion, pour onto a serving plate, and garnish with aonori and pickled ginger.

name.en: Seared Tuna Don (Maguro Tataki Rice Bowl)

en: Fresh tuna fillet 140 g
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and lemon juice 1 tsp
Grated ginger and 1 small crushed garlic clove
Cooked white rice 130 g
Cucumber and avocado, small cubes, 60 g total
Sesame seeds, spring onion and nori for garnish
Mix the soy sauce, lemon juice, ginger and garlic, marinate the tuna in half the mixture and keep the rest for serving.
Heat a very hot pan and sear the tuna 30-45 seconds per side only, until the surface colours while the centre stays rare.
Let it cool slightly and slice thinly.
Arrange the rice in a serving bowl, place the tuna slices on top with the cucumber and avocado, pour over the remaining sauce, and garnish with sesame, spring onion and nori.
150 g skinless chicken thigh
2 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp mirin
1 tsp sugar or honey
1 tsp oil, sesame seeds
Mix the soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a cup
Pan-fry the chicken in the oil 5 minutes per side
Add the sauce and simmer until glossy and thick
Slice and sprinkle with sesame seeds
100 g chicken breast, sliced
100 g tofu
Chinese cabbage, mushrooms, carrot
2 cups dashi stock
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sake
Heat the stock with the soy sauce and sake in a pot
Add the carrot and mushrooms, simmer 5 minutes
Add the chicken and cabbage, cook until done
Add the tofu at the end and warm 2 minutes
Mackerel or salmon fillet 140 g
Miso paste 1 tbsp
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tsp and mirin 1 tsp (or lemon juice as an alternative)
Half a tsp brown sugar
Cooked white rice 100 g
Spring onion and sesame for garnish
Mix the miso with the soy sauce, mirin and brown sugar until combined.
Brush the fish with the mixture and let it marinate 15-20 minutes.
Grill in a 220°C oven or under the broiler 10-12 minutes until cooked with light char marks.
Garnish with spring onion and sesame, and serve with the rice.

name.en: Nikujaga (Japanese Beef and Potato Stew) with Rice

en: Thin lean beef slices 100 g
Potato, cubed, 150 g
Carrot, sliced, 50 g
1 medium onion, sliced
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and brown sugar 1 tsp
Cooked white rice 100 g and water 200 ml
Stir the onion in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes, add the beef and stir until it changes colour.
Add the potato, carrot, water, soy sauce and brown sugar.
Cover and simmer 18-20 minutes until the potato is tender and the texture thickens.
Serve hot over the rice.
Very thinly sliced lean beef 110 g
Firm tofu, cubed, 50 g
Napa cabbage, shiitake mushrooms and spring onion, 150 g total
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and brown sugar 2 tsp
Water 150 ml and mirin 1 tsp (optional)
Cooked white rice 100 g
Heat a wide pot and add the soy sauce, water, brown sugar and mirin, bring to a boil.
Add the napa cabbage and mushrooms and cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add the beef and tofu, spreading the beef in the liquid without piling it, cook 3-4 minutes until fully done.
Garnish with spring onion, and serve hot with the rice.

name.en: Buta no Shogayaki (Ginger Pork) with Rice

en: Thinly sliced lean pork or chicken 140 g
Grated ginger 1 tbsp
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and mirin 1 tsp
Brown sugar 1 tsp
Cooked white rice 120 g
Shredded cabbage and cherry tomatoes for garnish
Mix the grated ginger with the soy sauce, mirin and brown sugar.
Marinate the meat slices in the mixture and let them sit 10 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan and cook the meat 2-3 minutes per side until cooked and the sauce thickens slightly.
Serve with the rice, shredded cabbage and cherry tomatoes.
Salmon fillet 140 g
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and mirin 1 tbsp
Brown sugar 1 tsp
Cooked white rice 110 g
Steamed broccoli to serve
Sesame seeds for garnish
Mix the soy sauce, mirin and brown sugar.
Heat a non-stick pan and cook the salmon skin-side down first for 3 minutes until crisp.
Flip and pour in the sauce, cook 3-4 more minutes, spooning the sauce over it, until it thickens and becomes glossy.
Serve over the rice with the steamed broccoli, sprinkle with sesame.

name.en: Chikuzenni (Japanese Braised Chicken and Vegetables) with Rice

en: Chicken breast, small pieces, 100 g
Carrot, taro (or potato), shiitake mushrooms and green beans, 150 g total
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and brown sugar 1 tsp
Water 150 ml and mirin 1 tsp (optional)
1 tsp oil
Cooked white rice 100 g
Heat the oil and stir the chicken until it changes colour.
Add the carrot, taro and mushrooms and stir for two minutes.
Add the soy sauce, brown sugar, water and mirin, cover and simmer 18-20 minutes until the vegetables are cooked.
Add the green beans and cook 5 more minutes uncovered until the texture thickens, and serve with the rice.

name.en: Baked Chicken Nanban with Tartar Sauce and Rice

en: Chicken breast, flattened, 140 g
Coarse breadcrumbs 30 g, 1 egg and 1 tbsp flour
Rice vinegar 2 tbsp, low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp and brown sugar 1 tbsp for the nanban sauce
Low-fat yogurt 40 g and chopped pickled cucumber 1 tbsp for the tartar sauce
Chopped spring onion
Cooked white rice 120 g
Coat the chicken in flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp, slice into strips.
Heat the rice vinegar, soy sauce and brown sugar until the sugar dissolves, dip the chicken strips into it briefly.
Mix the yogurt with the chopped pickle and spring onion for the tartar sauce, serve the chicken with the rice and tartar sauce on the side.

name.en: Butajiru (Pork and Root Vegetable Miso Soup) with Rice

en: Lean pork or chicken, thin slices, 90 g
Carrot, daikon radish and potato, chopped, 150 g total
Tofu, cubed, 40 g
Miso paste 2.5 tbsp
Water or dashi stock 400 ml
Cooked white rice 100 g and spring onion for garnish
Stir the meat in a dry pot over medium heat until it changes colour.
Add the carrot, daikon, potato and dashi water, cover and cook 15 minutes until the vegetables are done.
Dissolve the miso paste in a ladle of the hot stock, then return it to the pot, add the tofu.
Let the pot near a boil without boiling hard for two minutes, garnish with spring onion, and serve with the rice.
100 g cooked Japanese rice
20 g grilled salmon, flaked
A pinch of salt
A quarter sheet of nori
A pinch of sesame seeds
Wet your hands with water and rub with salt
Put half the rice on your palm and make a hollow
Place the salmon in the middle and cover with the rest
Shape into a triangle and wrap with nori
100 g frozen edamame pods
1 tsp coarse salt
Water for boiling
A pinch of pepper (optional)
Lemon zest (optional)
Bring water to a boil with half the salt
Add the pods and boil 4-5 minutes
Drain while they are still bright green and firm
Sprinkle the rest of the salt, serve warm or cold
Lean minced chicken or pork 100 g
Finely chopped cabbage 80 g and spring onion
Crushed garlic and grated ginger
12 ready-made gyoza wrappers (or thin dumpling wrappers)
Low-sodium soy sauce and salt
1 tsp oil for brushing
Mix the minced meat with the cabbage, spring onion, garlic, ginger and salt until well combined.
Place a teaspoon of filling in the centre of each wrapper, wet the edges with water and fold into a half-moon, pleating the edges.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush the tops with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes until golden and crisp on the bottom, and serve with soy sauce.
1 egg
Dashi stock or light chicken stock 120 ml
Half a tsp low-sodium soy sauce and a little salt
A small piece of cooked chicken breast, chopped (optional), 30 g
Sliced mushroom (optional) 20 g
Chopped spring onion for garnish
Beat the egg gently without creating too much froth, add the dashi stock, soy sauce and salt, and mix.
Strain the mixture to ensure smoothness, add the chicken and mushroom if desired to a small heatproof cup.
Pour the mixture over them, cover the cup with foil.
Steam over low heat 15-18 minutes until the texture sets like a soft custard, garnish with spring onion and serve warm.
Ready-made fried tofu pockets (aburaage) 4 pieces
Cooked white rice 120 g
Rice vinegar 1 tbsp, brown sugar 1 tsp and a little salt for the rice
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp, brown sugar 1 tbsp and water 100 ml to cook the pockets
Sesame seeds for garnish
Pickled ginger to serve (optional)
Simmer the tofu pockets in the soy sauce, brown sugar and water for 8-10 minutes until they absorb the flavour, let them cool.
Mix the hot rice with the rice vinegar, brown sugar and salt, let it cool slightly.
Gently squeeze each pocket of excess liquid, carefully open it and fill with the seasoned rice without pressing too hard.
Fold the edges to close, sprinkle with sesame, and serve with pickled ginger.
Chicken breast, cubed, 150 g
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp
Grated ginger and 1 small crushed garlic clove
Cornflour 2 tbsp
1 egg
1 tsp oil for brushing, and lemon to serve
Marinate the chicken in the soy sauce, ginger and garlic for 15-20 minutes.
Beat the egg and dip the chicken pieces in it, then coat them in the cornflour.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp, and serve with lemon wedges.
Firm tofu 150 g
Cornflour 2 tbsp
Dashi stock or light chicken stock 100 ml
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp and mirin 1 tsp
Grated spring onion and grated daikon for garnish
1 tsp oil for brushing
Pat the tofu dry with a paper towel and cut into large cubes.
Coat it in the cornflour until fully covered.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes until crisp, heat the dashi with the soy sauce and mirin and pour it over the tofu, garnish with spring onion and grated daikon.
Chicken breast, cubed, 150 g
Spring onion, cut into large pieces
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and mirin 1 tbsp
Brown sugar 1 tsp
Wooden skewers soaked in water
A pinch of ground red pepper (optional)
Mix the soy sauce, mirin and brown sugar.
Thread the chicken and spring onion alternately onto the skewers.
Grill under the broiler or in a 220°C oven 12-14 minutes, turning and brushing with the sauce several times, until cooked and glossy.
Sprinkle with red pepper if desired, and serve hot.

name.en: Baked Chicken Tsukune Skewers with Sweet Soy Glaze

en: Lean minced chicken 150 g
Finely chopped spring onion and grated ginger
Cornflour 1 tbsp and 1 egg white
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp, brown sugar 1 tbsp and mirin 1 tsp for the glaze
Small wooden skewers
Sesame for garnish
Knead the minced chicken with the spring onion, ginger, cornflour and egg white thoroughly until it binds together.
Wet your hands and shape the mixture into oval fingers around wooden skewers.
Arrange on a lined tray and bake at 220°C for 12-15 minutes until fully cooked.
Heat the soy sauce, brown sugar and mirin until it thickens slightly, brush the skewers with it and bake 3 more minutes, sprinkle with sesame and serve.
Cold silken or soft tofu 150 g
Finely chopped spring onion
Grated ginger
A pinch of shaved dried bonito flakes (katsuobushi) (optional)
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tsp
Sesame seeds for garnish
Chill the tofu well in the refrigerator before serving.
Cut it into one block or cubes and place on a serving plate.
Arrange the spring onion, ginger and bonito flakes on top.
Drizzle with soy sauce and sprinkle sesame, and serve immediately chilled.
1 cup natural fruit juice
2 g kanten (agar) powder
Chopped fruit (kiwi, strawberry)
1 tsp honey (optional)
Water
Dissolve the kanten in half a cup of water and boil 2 minutes
Add the juice and honey, stir well
Divide the fruit into cups and pour the liquid over
Chill for an hour until set
150 g Japanese sweet potato
1 tbsp kinako (roasted soybean flour)
1 tsp honey
A pinch of salt
A pinch of cinnamon (optional)
Wash the sweet potato and wrap it in baking paper
Bake at 180°C for 45 minutes
Split it lengthwise and fluff the flesh a little
Dust with kinako and salt, drizzle the honey
Whole-wheat flour 40 g
1 egg and 1 tsp honey
A quarter tsp baking powder
Sweet red bean paste (anko), low-sugar, 50 g
Water or low-fat milk 2 tbsp
1 tsp oil for cooking
Beat the egg with the honey until slightly frothy.
Gradually add the flour, baking powder and water until a smooth, pourable batter forms.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil and pour two small rounds of batter, cook 2 minutes until bubbles appear, flip and cook 1 more minute.
Repeat to get 4 rounds, place the bean paste between two rounds and close like a sandwich, repeat with the rest.
Glutinous rice flour (mochiko or shiratamako) 50 g
About 40 ml warm water
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp and brown sugar 2 tbsp
Half a tsp cornflour dissolved in 1 tbsp water
Water 50 ml for the sauce
Small wooden skewers (optional)
Knead the rice flour with the warm water gradually until you get a soft dough with the texture of an earlobe.
Shape into small balls, boil in boiling water 3-4 minutes until they float, then transfer to cold water.
Drain and thread onto skewers (3-4 balls per skewer) if desired.
Heat the soy sauce, brown sugar and water until it boils, add the dissolved cornflour and cook 1 minute until it thickens, pour it over the rice balls and serve.
Warabi starch (or cornflour as a substitute) 30 g
Water 180 ml
Brown sugar 2 tsp
Roasted soybean powder (kinako) 2 tbsp for coating
1 extra tsp brown sugar to mix with the kinako
A pinch of salt
Dissolve the starch with the brown sugar and salt in cold water until completely lump-free.
Heat it in a pot over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens and becomes translucent and sticky (5-7 minutes).
Pour into a water-moistened dish in an even layer, let it cool then chill in the fridge 30 minutes until set.
Cut into cubes, mix the kinako with the extra brown sugar and toss the cubes in it, and serve chilled.
2 eggs
Brown sugar 30 g and honey 1 tsp
Whole-wheat flour 40 g, sifted
1 tbsp warm water
1 tsp oil for greasing
A pinch of salt
Beat the eggs with the brown sugar, honey and salt with an electric whisk 5-7 minutes until the mixture becomes pale, thick and nearly doubles in volume.
Add the sifted flour in three batches, gently folding with a spoon until it disappears without deflating the mixture.
Add the warm water and fold gently, pour into a small tin greased with oil and lined with parchment.
Bake at 160°C for 25-30 minutes until cooked and it springs back when pressed gently, let cool completely before slicing.

name.en: Zenzai (Sweet Red Bean Soup with Mochi)

en: Cooked small red beans (azuki) 80 g
Water 150 ml
Brown sugar 30 g
A pinch of salt
2 small ready-made mochi (or glutinous rice flour 20 g to make them)
Toasted sesame seeds for garnish (optional)
Mash half the red beans and leave the other half whole.
Put them in a pot with the water, brown sugar and salt, simmer on low heat 10 minutes, stirring, until the texture thickens slightly.
If using ready-made mochi, toast it in a dry pan or toaster until it puffs up and turns light golden.
Place the mochi in a serving bowl and pour the bean soup over it, sprinkle with sesame and serve warm.
1 egg
Low-fat milk 120 ml
Brown sugar 15 g for the custard
Half a tsp vanilla extract
Brown sugar 20 g and water 2 tbsp for the caramel sauce
A drop of hot water for the caramel sauce

For the caramel: heat the brown sugar in a small pan over medium heat without stirring until it melts and turns dark golden, carefully add a drop of hot water (it will steam), and pour it into the bottom of a small heatproof cup.
Gently beat the egg with the milk, brown sugar and vanilla without creating too much froth.
Strain the mixture and pour it over the caramel in the cup, cover with foil.
Steam over very low heat 15-18 minutes until it sets like a soft custard, chill in the fridge for two hours, invert onto a serving plate before eating.

name.en: Anmitsu (Agar Jelly with Fruit and Sweet Red Bean)

en: Half a tsp agar agar powder
Water 200 ml
Fresh fruit, chopped (kiwi and orange) 80 g
Low-sugar sweet red bean paste (anko) 40 g
Light brown sugar syrup 1 tbsp
Poppy seeds or ground pistachios (optional)
Dissolve the agar powder in the water and boil over medium heat, stirring, for two minutes until fully dissolved.
Pour into a shallow dish and let it cool at room temperature, then chill in the fridge 30 minutes until set.
Cut the jelly into cubes, arrange in a serving bowl with the fruit and bean paste.
Pour the brown sugar syrup over it, sprinkle poppy seeds or pistachios if desired, and serve chilled.
Whole-wheat flour 40 g
1 egg and 1 tsp honey
A quarter tsp baking powder
Water or low-fat milk 3 tbsp
Low-sugar sweet red bean paste (anko) 60 g
1 tsp oil for brushing
Beat the egg with the honey, gradually add the flour, baking powder and water until a smooth, pourable batter forms.
Heat a small non-stick pan (or a large round pancake mould as a substitute) with a little oil.
Pour a thin layer of the batter, place a spoonful of the bean paste in the centre, cover with another layer of batter.
Cook over low heat 3-4 minutes per side until golden and fully cooked.
